technical_findings.category: Identity authority, atomic issuance, and provider revocation
technical_findings.description: The frozen device authorization design persists grants in JSON and coordinates them with sessions through a new process/file lock. The accepted modern-auth dependency instead makes auth.sqlite3 the sole Identity authority and requires proof consumption, fresh account/session/auth-version checks, and session issuance in one transaction. Its session rows carry auth_version, auth_method, and provider_binding_id, and provider revocation deletes sessions by binding. The proposed file lock is not observed by AuthStore transactions, while the CLI contract does not preserve the approving session's provider/version lineage. Consequently an exchange can race an auth-version change or provider unlink/revocation, and a newly issued CLI session can survive loss of the provider authority that approved it. This is an authorization and revocation hole, not merely an architecture preference.

technical_findings.recommendation: Reconcile the CLI authorization contract with the accepted modern Identity authority before implementation. Device grants must live under AuthStore with their bounded retention, purge, and export exclusion; approval/exchange must conditionally consume the grant and insert the CLI session in the same AuthStore transaction after fresh source-session, owner, deletion, auth_version, exposure, expiry, and provider-binding checks. Preserve the approving session's auth_version, auth_method, and provider_binding_id revocation lineage, or an equivalent binding enforced by the same transaction and foreign keys. Remove the independent JSON authority and flock design. Add deterministic races for provider unlink/revocation, auth-version changes, password reset, logout, and purge versus exchange.

technical_findings.description: The device contract says to call existing session minting but never defines how the new CLI session inherits the approving session's auth_method, provider_binding_id, and auth_version.
